title: Capital Credits (Patronage Capital) Training Notes: Account Status and Who Holds the Credits
content:
# Account Status and Who Holds the Credits

*Member services training notes — Capital Credits (Patronage Capital).*

**The rule.** A capital account becomes inactive on the final date of the member's last service account billed on a schedule of the class, and active again when the member connects service on such a schedule. An account becomes fully retired only when its unretired credits and its retired credits owed are both exactly zero. Moving, closing service or transferring a location to another member never moves capital credits to the new holder; they stay with the member who bought the power.

## The two balances on every capital account

- **Unretired credits** — patronage capital allocated to the member and not yet retired. Annual allocations add to it; general, estate and discounted early retirements reduce it by the gross allocated amount retired.
- **Retired credits owed** — retired capital credits owed to the member and not yet paid out, including amounts carried forward below the minimum payout. Each retirement adds its payable (after any discount) and a voided check adds its amount back; bill credits, checks, offsets, donations and escheats reduce it.

## The four statuses

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| active | the member still buys power in the class |
| inactive | the last service account billed in the class was final billed; the credits stay on the books until retired |
| estate claim pending | an estate retirement application for a deceased member or former member was taken with the certified death certificate on file |
| fully retired | nothing remains unretired or owed on the account |

## Questions answered

**When does a Farm Patron Class account go inactive if the member has two Schedule FH meters?** On the final date of the last of them; while either is still billed, the account stays active.

**A member who sold the farm asks whether the buyer now holds the credits.** No. Transferring a location to another member never moves the credits; they stay with the member who bought the power.

**An inactive account shows $0.00 unretired and $3.40 still owed. Is it fully retired?** No. Both balances must be exactly zero.

**What makes an inactive account active again?** The member connecting service again on a rate schedule of the class.

**What happens to an estate claim pending account when the application is withdrawn or denied?** It returns to inactive, and the credits return to the general rotation.
